one_month_reasoning: No CEG earnings expected inside the window: Q2 was reported Aug 6, so Q3 2026 results most likely land in early November (after 2026-10-29). Events in the window: PJM's one-time reliability backstop auction for new capacity runs Sept 30 to Oct 21 (results may or may not publish before Oct 29; a large, cheap clearing would reinforce the 'new supply caps scarcity rents' bear narrative, a small one the opposite); residual Calpine-holder (ECP/CPPIB/TRS, ~5.9% stake after the June secondary) selling could keep pressing supply; rates/utility-sector moves (Treasury yields were blamed for the Sept 9-18 13% drop). Stock just fell 7.1% on 9/29 in a broad risk-off session, so a mild short-term reversal is plausible but not strong enough to call. I stay close to symmetric: median ~$265.5 (slightly above last close for a small reversal tilt), monthly sigma ~13% (47% annual / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (2028E EPS $14.00 x 19x = $266, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM FCF/share ~$15.7 at a 6% yield = $262, weight 0.4); skeptic haircuts to management's growth path because ~30-35% of 2029 earnings are 'enhanced' by above-historical power prices and PJM capacity is capped at ~$325/MW-day.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E adjusted EPS $14.00 (forward EPS at the Sept-2027 horizon) x 19x

inputs_detail.derivation: Start at $12.00 guidance mid; management targets >10% base growth plus buybacks, which would give ~$14.5-15 for 2028. I haircut to ~8% CAGR because Q1-2027 consensus quarterly EPS falls ~4% y/y (source 5), PJM capacity revenue is capped at $325/MW-day through 2029/30 auctions (source 7), and a third of 2029 earnings depends on power prices/margins above historical levels (source 2).

Stock trades ~22x 2026 guidance and ~24x trailing per source 2; Citi's Neutral $297 target (source 3) and a ~$349 mean target (source 5) embed 21-25x. I use 19x: a de-rating toward IPP/merchant multiples as AI-premium fades and policy risk (emergency auction, price collar) persists, still above a pure merchant generator because ~contracted nuclear PPAs (920 MW new 15-20 yr deals) support duration.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF before growth ~$5.5B / ~350M shares = ~$15.7/share at a 6% required yield

inputs_detail.input: NTM FCF at horizon (Q4-2027 to Q3-2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Interpolating between ~$4.2B/yr (2026-27) and ~$6.1B/yr (2028-29), weighted toward 2028, then haircut ~5% for the enhanced-earnings/power-price exposure.
360M Q2 average diluted shares less ~10M from the remaining ~$2.8B buyback authorization at ~$270.

BBB+/Baa1 credit with ~$24B gross-less-cash debt (ST borrowings $5.2B + LTD $19.5B - cash $0.7B at 6/30/26) and merchant exposure: 6% yield is roughly a 200bp equity spread over IG power-company debt yields.

bear.story: Policy caps the scarcity rent: PJM price collar extended and emergency/backstop procurement plus new-build supply compress capacity and energy prices; hyperscaler contracting stays slow; 2028E EPS ~$12.5 and multiple de-rates to ~15x as the AI-power premium disappears. Continued Calpine-holder selling and higher rates add pressure.

base.story: Guidance delivered (2026 ~$12, 2027 ~$13), a few more long-term PPAs signed, Crane restart progresses toward 2027; multiple settles ~19-20x on 2028E ~$14. Stock grinds modestly higher with dividends/buybacks but no re-rating to the 2025 highs.

bull.story: Large hyperscaler deals announced once PJM's co-location/large-load framework is set, Crane online in 2027, power prices stay high; 2028E EPS ~$15.5 and multiple back to ~25x, toward the top of the $290-$441 analyst target range.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$195 (about 15% under the July 2026 low of $228.63 and ~14x 2027E EPS), the market would be pricing a structural earnings reset rather than overhang/rates noise: e.g., FERC/PJM rules that divert data-center load to new-build or regulated supply, a guidance cut, a Crane restart slip toward 2031, or a credit event (a loss of IG would require ~$3.4B of collateral).

catalysts.event: PJM one-time reliability backstop auction window (Sept 30 - Oct 21) closes; size/price of new capacity procured
Q3 2026 earnings; first read on 2027 guidance framework and buyback pace
Brazos Valley divestiture close ($860M) and DOJ approval; debt paydown
Q4 2026 results and formal 2027 EPS guidance
PJM/FERC large-load, co-location and capacity-market reform decisions; hyperscaler PPA announcements that were paused awaiting them
Crane Clean Energy Center restart (targeted 2027) under Microsoft PPA
Next PJM base residual auction results under the price collar
Further sales by former Calpine holders (5.9% stake after June secondary); securities-fraud and wage-fixing antitrust litigation

key_uncertainties: How much of current earnings is cyclical 'enhanced' power-price margin (management: 30-35% of 2029 earnings) versus durable contracted revenue
PJM/FERC and political intervention (price collar at ~$325/MW-day, emergency procurement, data-center cost allocation) capping upside
Pace of hyperscaler contracting, which management says customers paused awaiting PJM rules
Crane restart timing (FERC CIR waiver granted, but PJM earlier flagged a 2031 interconnection)
Supply overhang from former Calpine owners and sector sensitivity to Treasury yields
Leverage after Calpine (~$24B net debt incl. $5.2B short-term borrowings) if power prices fall
reasoning: Facts: CEG closed $264.58, down ~36% from the $412.70 high; 2026 adj. EPS guidance was raised to $11.50-12.50 on Q2 (Aug 6), so the stock is ~22x current-year EPS. The decline was driven less by earnings than by (1) policy: the Jan-2026 White House/governors push for an emergency PJM auction (CEG -9.7% that day), extension of the PJM capacity price collar through 2029/30 (July auction cleared at the $325 cap), and a DOE 202(c) emergency on June 30; (2) supply: Calpine sellers' $3.1B secondary in June and further sales in September; (3) Crane interconnection scare (PJM said 2031; FERC waiver in Q2 largely resolves this); (4) rates. Skeptic findings: management itself says 30-35% of 2029 earnings are 'enhanced' by above-historical prices/margins; Q1-2027 consensus EPS dips y/y; CEO sold ~$25M of stock at $272 in Feb-2026; hyperscaler deals are paused pending PJM rules; balance sheet has $5.2B of short-term borrowings and $3.4B of collateral exposure to an IG loss (ratings stable BBB+/Baa1, so low near-term risk); litigation (wage-fixing antitrust class action, law-firm 'investigations') looks like noise rather than thesis-changing. Weighing honestly: no accounting red flags, credit is stable, guidance is rising, and sell-side remains overwhelmingly Buy (mean target ~$349) - so the downside case is about multiple compression and policy, not fraud or distress. My fair value (~$265, 19x 2028E $14 and a 6% FCF yield) is roughly the current price, below consensus targets. Scenarios $185/$280/$390 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$284 (dividend excluded). For the ladder I use a lognormal centered at ~$272 median with ~38% sigma (below the 47% realized vol, which was inflated by one-off policy/overhang shocks, but well above the 25-35% large-cap base rate), and slightly fatten the left tail for policy/credit risk. Research limited to ~15 queries; several IR/press pages blocked (403/503), so the Q2 release was read from the SEC 8-K exhibit.
